Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but that memory explicitly flags a retention cost and warns against generalizing it as a growth strategy — verifying its archived record before ruling it out is worth the budget given how directly the competitive situation invites reaching for it anyway. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are solid but address neither of the two internal metrics currently declining, so they're lower priority for this week's single slot. Given only one experiment slot and a durable-revenue objective, I favor a guarded onboarding-simplification test to address the completion/activation decline without touching pricing-driven acquisition, which risks repeating the known retention tradeoff. I want to keep this small and guarded rather than a broad rollout since underlying causes of the metric declines (e.g., possible interaction with the competitor's pricing pull) aren't fully diagnosed yet.
